- Are you positioning Redwood as a data processor or controller for the hosted API we demoed?

- Can you provide your current SOC 2 report and a completed vendor security questionnaire (we can send our template).

If you can summarize those items and indicate next steps / timeline, we can kick off procurement and legal review.

Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 10:15:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick privacy question after today's demo

Hi all —

Thanks for the summary, Avery. High-level legal position and recommended approach below:

1) Controller / Processor: For hosted API use (Redwood-managed runtime) we are the processor; Oxbridge remains the controller. For Private/VPC/on-prem installs the roles can be adjusted in contract, but for this engagement (hosted) we should treat Redwood as processor in the DPA.

2) SCC module recommendation:
- Because Oxbridge is an EU-based controller contracting with a US-hosted processor, recommend we propose the SCC set with a processor-focused addendum (Module P / processor safeguards). That covers export legal basis + processing clauses without forcing controller obligations on Redwood.

3) DPA redlines to expect from legal:
- Data categories + purpose: ask Oxbridge to confirm exact data types (PII, payment metadata, etc.).
- Subprocessors: we'll provide our current list and a timely notice process for changes.
- Data retention & deletion: propose standard retention + deletion trigger on contract termination; if Oxbridge needs shorter retention windows we can negotiate but need specifics.
- Security evidence: SOC 2 report provided; we'll also offer a point-in-time architecture diagram on request under NDA.

Action items assigned:
- Laura (Legal): finalize DPA draft with processor SCC language and send redline-ready doc to Oxbridge by EOD 20 Aug 2026.
- David (Infra): publish current subprocessor list and confirm EU region residency options (and whether we can guarantee EU-only processing for this account) by EOD 20 Aug.
- Naomi (Security): plan to complete Oxbridge VSQ; please confirm estimated turnaround.

Marta — if you can share your VSQ template (or a procurement intake form) and confirm the primary data categories Oxbridge expects to send, that will speed review.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

--
Note: DPA draft will be shared as DPA_draft_Redwood_v1.docx (editable).
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@oxbridge-fin.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 15:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick privacy question after today's demo

Hi Laura / Avery —

Thanks, that all sounds good. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed: Oxbridge will be controller; Redwood will be processor for the hosted product.
- We prefer SCC language that explicitly maps to processor obligations (so Module P / processor addendum is preferred).
- Primary data categories: customer account identifiers, transaction metadata (no raw payment PANs in payloads), and support-case transcripts that may contain PII. We'll put formal categories in the VSQ.
- Data residency: Oxbridge prefers EU-only processing where feasible. Please confirm whether Redwood can guarantee EU-only processing for this workload or if any U.S. subprocessors will be involved.
- Procurement: we'll need the DPA + SOC2 and a completed VSQ before we can issue a PO.

Attached: Oxbridge_VSQ_Initial.xlsx (our template). Please confirm target dates for each action.

Best,
Marta
